newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-WALES STRUGGLE TO OVERCOME UNITED STATES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WALES STRUGGLE TO OVERCOME UNITED STATES.

text.p: Wales struggled to overcome the United States 34-14 on Saturday in an unconvincing warmup for the Five Nations' championship starting next weekend.
British Lions' wing Ieuan Evans scored a try in each half and there was another for caretaker captain Scott Gibbs. But overall Wales did not look like genuine championship contenders.

Wales, who take on Scotland in Edinburgh next Saturday, needed 14 points from fly-half Arwel Thomas to keep the spirited U.S. team at bay. Thomas kicked two penalties and converted each of the four tries.

Not even the introduction of Jonathan Davies and three other late substitutions could inspire Wales and the match ended in something of an anti-climax when a penalty try was awarded against U.S. number eight Rob Lumkong at a set scrum.

The United States, beaten 46-0 in their only previous visit to Cardiff, provided some of the match's outstanding moments, including a thrilling 70-metre move rounded off in spectacular fashion by scrum-half Andre Bachlelet.

Wales announce their team to meet Scotland on Monday and there could well be a recall for Davies at the expense of Thomas. He looked hesitant in attacking positions, although his place kicking was of the required class.
